problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. You can return the answer in any order.
problems.hint: Use a Hash Map to store numbers you have already visited and their indices: map.set(nums[i], i). For each number, check if (target - nums[i]) already exists in the map.
constraints: Follow-up: Can you come up with an algorithm that is less than O(n²) time complexity?

problems.title: Reverse a Linked List
problems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list represented as an array of values, reverse the list, and return the reversed array of values.
problems.hint: Use three pointers (prev = null, curr = head, next) or iteratively reverse the links in a single pass!
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is the range [0, 5000].

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description:
Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of brackets in the correct order.
problems.hint: Use a Stack! When encountering an opening bracket, push it. When encountering a closing bracket, check if it matches the top of the stack.

examples.explanation: All three pairs match in proper order.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.description:
You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists represented as arrays list1 and list2.

Merge the two lists into one sorted list and return it.
problems.hint: Use two pointers comparing list1[i] and list2[j], appending the smaller element to your result.
constraints: The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50].
Both list1 and list2 are sorted in non-decreasing order.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's)
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.
problems.hint: Kadane's Algorithm: Maintain currentMax = max(nums[i], currentMax + nums[i]), and update maxSoFar.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum 6.
The subarray [5, 4, -1, 7, 8] has the largest sum 23.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve by choosing a day to buy and a later day to sell. If no profit can be achieved, return 0.
problems.hint: Keep track of minPrice seen so far. At each day, calculate profit = price - minPrice.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6 - 1 = 5.
No transactions are done and max profit = 0.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
problems.hint: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). This is equivalent to the Fibonacci sequence!

examples.explanation: 1. 1 step + 1 step + 1 step\n2. 1 step + 2 steps\n3. 2 steps + 1 step

problems.title: Debug: Array Sum
problems.description: Fix the starting total in this function. Add every number exactly once.
problems.hint: The sum before reading any numbers should be zero.

lessons.title: Bubble Sort
lessons.summary: Compare neighbors. If the left number is bigger, swap them. Keep going until a full pass makes no swaps.
steps: Compare two neighbors.
Swap them if they are in the wrong order.
Repeat with the remaining numbers; stop when nothing changes.

lessons.title: Selection Sort
lessons.summary: Find the smallest remaining number and put it in the next empty sorted position.
steps: Scan the unsorted part for its smallest number.
Swap that number into the next sorted position.
Move the boundary one place to the right and repeat.

lessons.title: Insertion Sort
lessons.summary: Take one number and move it left until it fits among the already sorted numbers.
steps: Take the next number.
Compare it with the number to its left.
Move it left while it is smaller; repeat for the next number.

lessons.title: Merge Sort
lessons.summary: Split the list into smaller lists. Sort them, then combine them by always taking the smaller front number.
steps: Split until each piece contains one number.
Compare the fronts of two pieces.
Take the smaller front until both pieces are merged.

lessons.title: Quick Sort
lessons.summary: Pick a pivot. Move smaller numbers before it and larger numbers after it. Sort both sides the same way.
steps: Choose the last number as the pivot.
Move smaller numbers to the left and place the pivot.
Repeat separately on the left and right sides.

lessons.title: Radix Sort
lessons.summary: Sort numbers by their ones digit, then tens digit, then hundreds digit. Keep the order of numbers with the same digit.
steps: Put numbers into digit buckets 0 through 9.
Collect the buckets in order without rearranging a bucket.
Repeat for the next digit until all digits are handled.

lessons.title: Linear Search
lessons.summary: Check each number from left to right until you find the target or run out of numbers.
steps: Check the current number.
If it matches, stop.
Otherwise move right; report not found at the end.

lessons.title: Binary Search
lessons.summary: On a sorted list, check the middle. Keep only the half where your target can still be.
steps: Start with a sorted list.
Check the middle number.
Keep the left or right half; repeat until found or the range is empty.

lessons.title: Array Traversal
lessons.summary: Visit every position in an array, in order.
steps: Start at position zero.
Read the value at the current position.
Advance one position until the end.

lessons.title: Sliding Window Sum
lessons.summary: Keep a group of k neighbors. Slide it right by removing the old left value and adding the new right value.
steps: Add the first k values.
Record the sum for this window.
Subtract the outgoing value, add the incoming value, and repeat.

lessons.title: Two-Pointer Pair Sum
lessons.summary: On sorted numbers, put one finger at each end. Move the left finger to increase the sum, or the right finger to decrease it.
steps: Sort the values and place pointers at the ends.
Compare their sum with the target.
Move the appropriate pointer until a pair is found or pointers meet.

lessons.title: Reverse a String
lessons.summary: Swap the first and last letters, then work toward the middle.
steps: Place pointers at the first and last letter.
Swap those two letters.
Move both pointers inward until they meet.

lessons.title: Stack: Push & Pop
lessons.summary: Add and remove items at the top. The last item added is the first one removed.
steps: Push the values onto the top one at a time.
Read the top value.
Pop values from the top until empty.

lessons.title: Queue: Enqueue & Dequeue
lessons.summary: Add at the back and remove from the front. The first item added is the first one removed.
steps: Enqueue each value at the back.
Read the front value.
Dequeue from the front until empty.

lessons.title: Deque: Both Ends
lessons.summary: A deque lets you add or remove an item at either end.
steps: Alternate adding values at the front and back.
Observe both ends.
Alternate removing from the front and back.

lessons.title: Priority Queue
lessons.summary: Remove the smallest value first, regardless of when it arrived. A min-heap keeps the smallest value at its root.
steps: Insert a value at the end of the heap.
Move it upward while it is smaller than its parent.
Remove the root, replace it with the last value, then repair the heap.

lessons.title: Singly Linked List
lessons.summary: Each node stores a value and a link to the next node. Start at the head and follow the links.
steps: Append a node by linking the previous tail to it.
Start at the head node.
Follow next links until reaching null.

lessons.title: Doubly Linked List
lessons.summary: Each node links to the next and previous node, so you can walk in either direction.
steps: Connect a new node to the previous tail in both directions.
Follow next links from head to tail.
Follow previous links from tail to head.

lessons.title: Circular Linked List
lessons.summary: The last node links back to the first node. Stop after a full round so you do not loop forever.
steps: Link the values into a list.
Point the tail back to the head.
Follow exactly n links to complete one round.

lessons.title: Binary Search Tree
lessons.summary: Smaller values go left and larger values go right. Follow that rule to insert or find a value.
steps: Start at the root.
Compare: smaller goes left, larger goes right.
Insert at an empty link or stop at the matching value.

lessons.title: Tree Breadth-First Traversal
lessons.summary: Visit the root, then its children, then their children. Use a queue to remember the next nodes.
steps: Put the root in a queue.
Remove and visit the front node.
Add its children to the back and repeat.

lessons.title: Tree Depth-First Traversal
lessons.summary: Visit a node, explore its left branch completely, then explore its right branch.
steps: Visit the current node.
Explore its left child recursively.
Explore its right child recursively.

lessons.title: AVL Tree Insertion
lessons.summary: An AVL tree keeps its left and right heights within one level. Rotate an unbalanced branch after inserting.
steps: Insert using the binary-search-tree rule.
Check the left and right heights on the way back up.
Rotate the leaning branch; use two rotations for a zigzag.

lessons.title: Red-Black Tree Insertion
lessons.summary: Use red and black node colors to keep search paths roughly balanced. Repair colors and rotate after inserting.
steps: Insert the new value as a red node.
Fix two red nodes in a row by recoloring or rotating.
Keep the root black and equal black counts along every path.

lessons.title: Min-Heap Construction
lessons.summary: A parent is never larger than its children. Insert at the end and move a small value upward until the rule holds.
steps: Insert at the next open leaf.
Compare with its parent.
Swap upward while the parent is bigger.

lessons.title: Graph Breadth-First Search
lessons.summary: Visit nearby nodes first. A queue makes you finish one distance level before moving farther away.
steps: Mark the start and put it in a queue.
Visit the front node.
Queue its unvisited neighbors; repeat.

lessons.title: Graph Depth-First Search
lessons.summary: Follow one path as far as possible. Mark visited nodes so cycles do not trap you.
steps: Mark and visit the current node.
Recursively explore an unvisited neighbor.
Backtrack and try the next neighbor.

lessons.title: Dijkstra Shortest Paths
lessons.summary: Repeatedly choose the unvisited node with the smallest known distance. Check whether going through it improves a neighbor’s distance.
steps: Set the start distance to zero and others to infinity.
Choose the unvisited node with the smallest distance.
Update its neighbors with cheaper routes; repeat.

lessons.title: Topological Sort
lessons.summary: Complete tasks that have no unfinished prerequisites. Remove their outgoing links to unlock more tasks.
steps: Count each node’s incoming edges.
Queue nodes with zero incoming edges.
Remove one, reduce its neighbors’ counts, and queue newly unlocked nodes.

lessons.title: Fibonacci: Tabulation
lessons.summary: Save the first two answers, then build each next answer by adding the previous two.
steps: Store F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.
For each i, calculate F(i) = F(i−1) + F(i−2).
Read the saved answer at n.

lessons.title: Fibonacci: Memoization
lessons.summary: Ask for the answer recursively. When a smaller answer is computed, save it so later calls can reuse it.
steps: Ask for F(n).
If an answer is saved, reuse it.
Otherwise solve the two smaller problems, add them, and save the result.

lessons.title: 0/1 Knapsack
lessons.summary: For each item and capacity, choose the better of skipping the item or taking it once.
steps: Start with no items and zero value.
For each item, compare skipping it with taking it if it fits.
Save the better answer; use the last row at full capacity.

lessons.title: Hash Map: Chaining
lessons.summary: A hash function chooses a bucket. If several keys choose the same bucket, keep them together in a small list. This map saves a frequency count for each key.
steps: Calculate bucket = key modulo 7.
Check that bucket for an existing key.
Insert a new key into its bucket, then search the target bucket.

lessons.title: Hash Map: Linear Probing
lessons.summary: If a key’s chosen slot is full, try the next slot until finding a free one. Search follows the same path. This map saves a frequency count for each key.
steps: Hash the key into the table.
If occupied, move one slot forward, wrapping around.
Insert in a free slot; search until matching or finding an empty slot.

lessons.title: Hash Set: Unique Values
lessons.summary: Store each value once. Hashing lets you check whether a value is already present.
steps: Hash each value to its bucket.
Check whether it is already stored.
Skip duplicates and keep only new values.
